name: Federal Way
seo_title: 7 Christmas Events for Kids in Federal Way, WA 2026
seo_desc: 7 Christmas events for kids in Federal Way, WA, 4 free: Jeanne Burbidge Holiday Festival at the Federal Way PAEC and more.
lede: Federal Way does Christmas around Town Square Park and the Performing Arts and Event Center next door, with a tree lighting led by the Mayor, a free holiday festival, a Nutcracker run and a rare after dark night at the Pacific Bonsai Museum.
celebrates: Most of Federal Way's holiday season happens on Pete von Reichbauer Way South. City of Federal Way Parks and Recreation holds the annual Holiday Tree Lighting in Town Square Park, with Santa, live music, hot cocoa and cookies before the Mayor lights the tree. Next door, the Performing Arts and Event Center hosts a free holiday festival, now named for Jeanne Burbidge, and The Nutcracker by Children's Dance Theater Foundation. The Federal Way Community Center adds the Jingle Bell Brunch and Cookies with Mrs. Claus, and the city runs a Wishing Tree for holiday requests. Across town, Pacific Bonsai Museum opens after dark once a year for its Winter Bonsai Solstice.
lastyear: In 2025 the Federal Way Symphony played its annual holiday concert, Celebrating the Holidays, at the Performing Arts and Event Center on Saturday, December 6, at 2:30 pm, with the Federal Way Chorale and a young Emerging Artist. The PAEC said the city's tree lighting ceremony would follow immediately in Town Square Park. That same Saturday, Sound Transit opened light rail to Federal Way, adding Kent Des Moines, Star Lake and Federal Way Downtown stations on the 1 Line.
facts: Federal Way is named for a highway. In 1929 five small school districts merged into Federal Way School District 210, the first official use of the name, which came from U.S. Route 99, the federal highway now called Pacific Highway South. The city itself is young: voters approved incorporation and the City of Federal Way began on February 28, 1990, with the official act held at the Sportsworld Lanes bowling complex. In 1962 a holiday themed amusement park called SantaFair opened in the area with more than 75 carnival rides.
trains: Sound Transit opened the Link 1 Line extension on December 6, 2025, with Star Lake Station near South 272nd Street and Federal Way Downtown Station at the Federal Way Transit Center, which serves the Performing Arts and Event Center. Trains now run north to Sea Tac Airport and Seattle. Back in 1902 the Seattle Tacoma Interurban ran along what is now Jovita Boulevard near Federal Way. For a train day, the Washington State History Museum in Tacoma has a big model railroad, and the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie runs its Santa Train.

traditions: Holiday Tree Lighting at Town Square Park
City Parks and Recreation gathers families for Santa, live music, cocoa and cookies before the Mayor lights the tree.
The Performing Arts and Event Center opens its doors for a free family festival with Mr. and Mrs. Claus, crafts and a Kids Market, now named for Jeanne Burbidge.

kidfact: Federal Way is named after a road. The old highway through town was a federal highway, U.S. Route 99, so when the schools joined together in 1929 they called themselves Federal Way.
faq: Where is the Federal Way Christmas tree lighting?

The City of Federal Way lights its tree in Town Square Park at 31600 Pete von Reichbauer Way South, right next to the Performing Arts and Event Center. City Parks and Recreation hosts it with a visit from Santa, live holiday music, hot cocoa and cookies, and the Mayor's annual tree lighting. The city lists it as a free event.
Can we take light rail to Christmas events in Federal Way?

Yes. Since December 6, 2025, Link 1 Line trains stop at Federal Way Downtown Station at the Federal Way Transit Center, which Sound Transit says serves the Performing Arts and Event Center. Town Square Park is beside the PAEC, so the tree lighting, the holiday festival and The Nutcracker are all close to the station.
Is there a Nutcracker in Federal Way?

Yes. Children's Dance Theater Foundation performs The Nutcracker at the Federal Way Performing Arts and Event Center each December, with two casts named Gum Drop and Ribbon Candy. The ballet runs about 90 minutes with an intermission. Children 3 and up need their own seat, and children 2 and under may sit on a lap.
What is the Winter Bonsai Solstice?

It is the one night a year Pacific Bonsai Museum in Federal Way opens after dark. The bonsai collection glows with soft holiday lights, hot chocolate is served free, and local artisans join the museum store for a small market. Admission is free thanks to 4Culture, and the museum suggests bringing a flashlight for the paths.
Why is it called Federal Way?

The name dates to 1929, when five school districts merged into Federal Way School District 210. It came from U.S. Route 99, a federally designated highway that ran through the area and is now Pacific Highway South. The local chamber of commerce adopted the name in the early 1950s, and the city incorporated on February 28, 1990.
